transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function for the Rust 1.96 target body.

Adapted the inherent [T] mutable receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` parameter and named return for Verus; the executable target body remains the single call SplitInclusiveMut::new(slice, pred).

Extracted the target-local SplitInclusiveMut representation with private mutable slice, predicate, and finished fields, preserving field names, order, types, and privacy while omitting Rust stability/doc attributes.
Included SplitInclusiveMut::new with the real Rust body `let finished = slice.is_empty(); Self { v: slice, pred, finished }` so the private constructor state is checked rather than trusted.
Preserved the Rust callback bound F: FnMut(&T) -> bool; the harness never invokes the callback in the constructor proof and uses only the audited fnmut_predicate_observed vocabulary.

Defined the local iterator-view helper over the extracted mutable initial iterator state to expose old source, remaining, empty yielded prefix/remainder, inclusive forward direction, zero limit, and predicate-observation lawfulness.

Revealed the closed iterator-view definition in ghost proof blocks and added a trigger to the local predicate-observation quantifier; these are proof-only annotations with no executable data-flow effect.
Actual Verus verifies the executable source-backed harness after the repaired generated contract removed the unsound final(slice)@ == old(slice)@ frame.
